sections.label: Cyberattacks and CII sectors
sections.summary: The passage cites cyberattack examples abroad and identifies CII in 11 sectors, urging government involvement with CII owners.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Communications and Information (Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim)
sentences.text: As we have seen in other countries, such cyberattacks can have a debilitating impact on the economy and society: (a) last year, the United Kingdom's (UK’s) National Health Service (NHS) had to cancel at least 6,900 appointments due to the WannaCry ransomware attack; (b) in the Ukrainian capital of Kiev, the power grids were hacked twice by cyberattackers in 2015 and 2016, leading to power disruptions that affected over 200,000 citizens during winter; and (c) in 2015, a massive cyberattack that reportedly intended to destroy important national communication channels took the French television (TV) network, TV5Monde, off the air for several hours.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Communications and Information (Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim)
sentences.text: There is an urgent need for the Government to be more actively involved with the CII owners in defending against cyberattacks.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Communications and Information (Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim)
sentences.text: We have identified CII in 11 sectors: Energy; Water; Banking and Finance; Healthcare; Transport which includes Land, Maritime, and Aviation; Infocomm, Media and Security and Emergency Services, and Government.

sections.label: Cybersecurity Bill objectives
sections.summary: The Cybersecurity Bill seeks a legal framework for national cybersecurity, with three objectives including protecting CII and licensing providers.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Communications and Information (Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim)
sentences.text: However, CMCA, which mainly deals with cybercrimes, such as the unauthorised access of computer material, does not provide a regulatory framework for the routine and proactive protection of CII.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Communications and Information (Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim)
sentences.text: Therefore, the Cybersecurity Bill seeks to establish a legal framework for the oversight and maintenance of national cybersecurity in Singapore, with an emphasis on the proactive protection of CII against cyberattacks.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Communications and Information (Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim)
sentences.text: The Bill has three key objectives: (a) to strengthen the protection of CII against cyberattacks; (b) to authorise the Cyber Security Agency of Singapore (CSA) to prevent and respond to cybersecurity threats and incidents; and (c) to establish a licensing framework for cybersecurity service providers.

sections.label: CSA powers over CII
sections.summary: The Bill gives CSA powers to proactively protect CII and respond to cybersecurity threats and incidents.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Communications and Information (Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim)
sentences.text: The Cybersecurity Bill will provide CSA with the necessary powers to proactively protect our CII and respond to cybersecurity threats and incidents.

sections.label: CII owners' statutory obligations
sections.summary: All CII owners face the same statutory obligations, including furnishing information, complying with directions, reporting incidents, audits and exercises.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Communications and Information (Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim)
sentences.text: All owners of CII, whether from the public or private sector, will be subjected to the same statutory obligations under the Bill.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Communications and Information (Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim)
sentences.text: These obligations include furnishing primarily technical information relating to CII (clause 10); complying with codes of practice and standards of performance (clause 11); complying with written directions (clause 12); informing the Commissioner of the change in the ownership of CII (clause 13); reporting cybersecurity incidents in respect of CII (clause 14); conducting cybersecurity audits and risk assessments of CII (clause 15); and finally, participating in cybersecurity exercises (clause 16).

sections.label: Maximum penalty stated
sections.summary: The maximum penalty is $100,000, or two years' imprisonment, or both.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Communications and Information (Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim)
sentences.text: The maximum penalty is $100,000, or two years’ imprisonment, or both.

sections.label: Powers for non-CII systems
sections.summary: Powers to respond to threats affecting CII will also be used to investigate major threats on non-CII computer systems.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Communications and Information (Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim)
sentences.text: The key intent is to provide for powers to respond to cybersecurity threats or incidents affecting CII.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Communications and Information (Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim)
sentences.text: But because of the interconnected nature of computer systems, the powers will also be used for investigating major cybersecurity threats and incidents on computer systems that are not CII, for example, large-scale cyberattacks affecting multiple sectors.

sections.label: Commissioner taking possession of computers
sections.summary: The Commissioner may take possession of a computer without consent if necessary, least disruptive, and benefits outweigh detriments.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Communications and Information (Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim)
sentences.text: The Commissioner may, under clause 20(5), take possession of any computer or equipment without the owner’s consent for the purpose of further examination and analysis, if the Commissioner is satisfied that: (a) this is necessary for the purpose of the investigation; (b) there is no less disruptive method of achieving the purpose of the investigation; and (c) after consultation with the owner, and after considering his business and operational needs, the benefit from doing so outweighs the detriment caused to him.

sections.label: Penalty for clause 20 offences
sections.summary: The maximum penalty under clause 20(7) is a $25,000 fine or two years' imprisonment or both.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Communications and Information (Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim)
sentences.text: The maximum penalty under clause 20(7) is $25,000 fine or two years’ imprisonment or both, for offences, such as failure without reasonable excuse to comply with a direction or requirement of an incident response officer, under clause 20(2)(b) or (c).

sections.label: Two licensed cybersecurity service types
sections.summary: Only penetration testing and managed security operations centre monitoring providers will be licensed.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Communications and Information (Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim)
sentences.text: Only providers of two types of cybersecurity services will be licensed, namely, penetration testing and managed security operations centre (SOC) monitoring.

sections.label: Maximum penalty stated
sections.summary: The maximum penalty is a $50,000 fine, or two years' imprisonment, or both.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Communications and Information (Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim)
sentences.text: The maximum penalty is a $50,000 fine, or two years’ imprisonment, or both.

sections.label: Appeals and CII designation process
sections.summary: Cybersecurity service providers may appeal to the Minister, and CSA will designate CII in consultation with owners and regulators.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Communications and Information (Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim)
sentences.text: Under clause 35, cybersecurity service providers may appeal to the Minister against specific decisions of the licensing officer, such as the refusal to grant a licence and licensing conditions.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Communications and Information (Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim)
sentences.text: CSA will adopt a deliberate process for the designation of CII across the different sectors, in consultation with their owners and the relevant sector regulators where possible.

sections.label: Bill purpose and licensing timing
sections.summary: The licensing framework will be operationalised later, and the Bill empowers CSA and establishes a licensing framework.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Communications and Information (Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim)
sentences.text: The licensing framework will be operationalised at a later stage, after the rest of the Bill.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Communications and Information (Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim)
sentences.text: With cyber threats growing globally, this Bill is timely to empower CSA to safeguard essential services from disruptions by cyberattacks, prevent and respond to cybersecurity threats and incidents, and to establish a licensing framework to improve the credibility of cybersecurity services in Singapore.

sections.label: Ukrainian electricity distribution cyberattack
sections.summary: On 23 December 2015, hackers took control of three Ukrainian electricity distribution companies' control centres and opened breakers, cutting power to over 200,000 households.

sentences.speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad (Chua Chu Kang)
sentences.text: On 23 December 2015, the control centres of three Ukrainian electricity distribution companies were taken control of, where malicious hackers opened breakers which caused more than 200,000 households to lose power.

sections.label: Singapore cyberattacks on critical sectors
sections.summary: CSA reported in September last year that several critical sectors faced cyberattacks and the Singapore Government faced a malware attack by state-sponsored hackers.

sentences.speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad (Chua Chu Kang)
sentences.text: While similar attacks have not shown to be highly-motivated acts of sabotage in Singapore, in September last year, CSA had reported that several critical sectors were subjected to cyberattacks, and that the Singapore Government had been subjected to a malware attack by state-sponsored hackers.

sections.label: Benchmarks or checklist for CIIs
sections.summary: The passage asks whether the Ministry will provide CIIs with specific benchmarks or a checklist of cybersecurity measures.

sentences.speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad (Chua Chu Kang)
sentences.text: This may be too late if an incident happens.

sentences.speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad (Chua Chu Kang)
sentences.text: So, will the Ministry be providing the CIIs with specific benchmarks they need to achieve or a checklist of cybersecurity measures that need to be in place?

sections.label: Cybersecurity Bill cost and authority
sections.summary: The passage asks if the Ministry estimated CII compliance costs, and notes the Bill gives the Minister, Commissioner and deputies authority to investigate and obtain CII information.

sentences.speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad (Chua Chu Kang)
sentences.text: Has the Ministry estimated how much it will cost for the CIIs to comply with the Cybersecurity Bill's requirements?

sentences.speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad (Chua Chu Kang)
sentences.text: Under the Cybersecurity Bill, the Minister, the Commissioner and his deputies are given the authority to investigate and get CIIs to disclose information to assist with investigations.

sections.label: CIIs defined by Singapore systems
sections.summary: Currently, CIIs are defined based on systems located in Singapore.

sentences.speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad (Chua Chu Kang)
sentences.text: Currently, the CIIs are defined based on systems located here in Singapore.

sections.label: CSA registration of companies not individuals
sections.summary: The passage says this promotes better trained service providers, and asks why CSA registers companies but does not license or register individuals.

sentences.speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad (Chua Chu Kang)
sentences.text: This will also promote our service providers to be better trained and specialised to meet the standards required by the regulators.

sentences.speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad (Chua Chu Kang)
sentences.text: However, I would like to seek clarity from the Minister why does CSA only register companies and not allow for the licensing or registration of individuals.

sections.label: Digital defence sixth pillar
sections.summary: A speaker suggests adding a sixth Total Defence pillar for cybersecurity or digital defence, citing loss of private information and industry feedback on the Bill.

sentences.speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad (Chua Chu Kang)
sentences.text: Perhaps, it may be time to add a sixth pillar to our Total Defence framework in the area of cybersecurity or digital defence to counter the new threats in this digital era.

sentences.speaker: Mr Pritam Singh (Aljunied)
sentences.text: More specifically, the loss or exposure of private information may also erode trust in the Government, statutory agencies and private companies as the release of such information in the public realm can seldom ever be completely reversed.

sentences.speaker: Mr Pritam Singh (Aljunied)
sentences.text: I understand the Bill has received significant feedback from industry with an excess of 60 companies, many of them large corporates, and separately, a healthy number of industry associations – not forgetting civic-conscious and interested individuals – providing feedback to the Ministry on this Bill.

sections.label: Compliance costs for CIIs
sections.summary: A speaker asks the Minister to estimate the dollar value of Cybersecurity Bill compliance costs for CIIs such as CAAS, PUB and public hospitals.

sentences.speaker: Mr Pritam Singh (Aljunied)
sentences.text: Can the Minister give us some sense or an estimate of the dollar value of the compliance costs of the Cybersecurity Bill with regard to, for example, CIIs in sectors referred to in Schedule 1 of the Bill – perhaps those covering the Civil Aviation Authority of Singapore (CAAS), the Public Utilities Board (PUB) and some public hospitals?

sections.label: Punishment for Uber breach
sections.summary: A speaker asks what punishment the Bill would effect against a company like Uber for compromising and concealing personal information of close to 380,000 Singaporeans.

sentences.speaker: Mr Pritam Singh (Aljunied)
sentences.text: With this as a backdrop, can the Minister also share with Parliament what punishment would be effected by this Bill against a company like Uber – assuming it is a CII – which caused the compromise of personal information, such as names, email addresses and personal contact numbers, of close to 380,000 Singaporeans and tried to conceal the same, as reported in November last year?

sections.label: Non-compliance penalties
sections.summary: Non-compliance carries a fine of up to $5,000 and/or imprisonment of up to six months.

sentences.speaker: Mr Pritam Singh (Aljunied)
sentences.text: Non-compliance carries with it a fine of up to $5,000 and/or an imprisonment term of up to six months.

sections.label: Protecting Singaporeans online
sections.summary: A speaker asks what measures Singaporeans can expect from the Government against cybersecurity threats, noting almost two billion records stolen in the first six months of 2017.

sentences.speaker: Mr Pritam Singh (Aljunied)
sentences.text: The CSA is in a privileged position to educate Singaporeans on security tips as we transition to a more cashless economy and live online, as many of us already do.

sentences.speaker: Mr Pritam Singh (Aljunied)
sentences.text: What measures can Singaporeans look forward from the Government to protect them from cybersecurity threats in our Smart Nation journey?

sentences.speaker: Mr Christopher de Souza (Holland-Bukit Timah)
sentences.text: Even within the first six months of 2017, the number of records stolen in breaches numbered almost two billion – even more than the whole of 2016, which was 1.4 billion.

sections.label: WannaCry in England
sections.summary: WannaCry, the first ransomware worm, shut down computers in over 80 NHS organisations in England, cancelling almost 20,000 appointments and diverting ambulances at five hospitals.

sentences.speaker: Mr Christopher de Souza (Holland-Bukit Timah)
sentences.text: WannaCry, the first ransomware worm, crippled the healthcare system in England.

sentences.speaker: Mr Christopher de Souza (Holland-Bukit Timah)
sentences.text: It "shut down computers in more than 80 NHS organisations in England alone", cancelling almost 20,000 appointments in an appointment-based healthcare system, five hospitals resorted to diverting ambulances, unable to handle any more emergency cases.

sections.label: MINDEF personnel data stolen 2017
sections.summary: In 2017, 850 MINDEF personnel had NRIC numbers, birth dates and telephone numbers stolen in a cyberattack.

sentences.speaker: Mr Christopher de Souza (Holland-Bukit Timah)
sentences.text: In 2017, 850 Ministry of Defence (MINDEF) personnel’s National Registration Identity Card (NRIC) numbers, birth dates and telephone numbers were stolen following a cyberattack.

sections.label: Bill regulatory framework key features
sections.summary: The Bill's framework includes breach reporting and investigation, licensing of cybersecurity service providers, and regular auditing.

sentences.speaker: Mr Christopher de Souza (Holland-Bukit Timah)
sentences.text: Some key features of this Bill’s regulatory framework include: (a) reporting and investigating of breaches to facilitate damage control and prevent future occurrences under clauses 14, 19 and 20; (b) licensing of cybersecurity service providers in Part 5; and (c) regular auditing under clause 15 to ensure compliance and accountability.

sections.label: Clause 3 extends regulation to networks
sections.summary: Clause 3 extends regulation to computer networks wholly or partly in Singapore, with a consistent yet flexible framework.

sentences.speaker: Mr Christopher de Souza (Holland-Bukit Timah)
sentences.text: Since computer networks extend beyond territorial boundaries and cyberattacks know no physical boundaries, clause 3 of this Bill extends regulation to computer networks that are wholly or partly in Singapore.

sentences.speaker: Mr Christopher de Souza (Holland-Bukit Timah)
sentences.text: This Bill has been carefully calibrated for a consistent framework over the different sectors yet providing space for flexibility for purpose-oriented, sector-suited rules and practices.

sections.label: Cost and white hats question
sections.summary: The estimated $100,000 cost is compared to up to a million dollars for a dedicated vulnerability assessment team, and the Bill complements the CMCA.

sentences.speaker: Mr Christopher de Souza (Holland-Bukit Timah)
sentences.text: The non-prohibitive cost estimated at $100,000, compared to up to a million dollars for hiring a dedicated vulnerability assessment team.

sentences.speaker: Mr Christopher de Souza (Holland-Bukit Timah)
sentences.text: Would the Minister clarify how this Bill would affect non-mainstream methods of strengthening cybersecurity, such as white hats?

sentences.speaker: Mr Christopher de Souza (Holland-Bukit Timah)
sentences.text: In this fast-changing technology-connected world, this Bill provides the preventive complement to the deterrent CMCA.

sections.label: Eleven key sectors and public consultation
sections.summary: Eleven key sectors are highlighted as critical, and the public consultation on the Bill was extended beyond 3 August 2017.

sentences.speaker: Ms K Thanaletchimi (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: The special focus of the 11 key sectors, such as Government, security and emergency, healthcare, telecommunications, banking and finance, energy, water, media, land transport, air transport and maritime, demonstrates the critical nature of the sector that could cripple the entire Singapore in terms of economy and threaten our lives to its devastation.

sentences.speaker: Ms K Thanaletchimi (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: With this as backdrop, I am, indeed, heartened to see the Government’s inclusive effort to garner stakeholder’s feedback and support on the Cybersecurity Bill.

sentences.speaker: Ms K Thanaletchimi (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: It is, indeed, notable that the public consultation on the Bill, which was originally scheduled from 10 July to 3 August 2017, was extended to allow respondents more time to provide feedback on such an important Bill that is pertinent to safeguard the people of Singapore in all aspects.

sections.label: SMEs resources and financial support
sections.summary: SMEs may lack resources and capabilities to adhere to the measures unless given impetus and financial support.

sentences.speaker: Ms K Thanaletchimi (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: SMEs may not have the resources and capabilities to adhere to the measures, unless they are given the impetus and financial support to put in place the necessary requirements.

sections.label: National cybersecurity audit proposal
sections.summary: A national cybersecurity audit checking stakeholders of the 11 sectors would give high assurance to those using services in the specific sector.

sentences.speaker: Ms K Thanaletchimi (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: Establishing a national cybersecurity audit to check on the stakeholders of the 11 sectors will provide a high level of assurance for those who engage in services in the specific sector.

sections.label: Singapore Cybersecurity Strategy pillars
sections.summary: The Paper setting out Singapore's Cybersecurity Strategy was published in October 2016 and has four pillars.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Daniel Goh Pei Siong (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: The Paper setting out Singapore’s Cybersecurity Strategy was published more than a year ago in October 2016.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Daniel Goh Pei Siong (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: The strategy has four pillars: building a resilient infrastructure, creating a safer cyberspace, developing a vibrant cybersecurity ecosystem and strengthening international partnerships.

sections.label: Israel cybersecurity companies
sections.summary: Israel is ahead in this game, with an estimated 420 cybersecurity companies today, many innovating and exporting technology.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Daniel Goh Pei Siong (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: Israel is already ahead of everyone in this game and there are an estimated 420 cybersecurity companies in Israel today, many of which are at the forefront of innovation and exporting their technology.

sections.label: NUS and NTU cyberattacks
sections.summary: NUS and NTU both suffered separate cyberattacks in April last year.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Daniel Goh Pei Siong (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: First, it was reported that the NUS and NTU both suffered separate cyberattacks in April last year.

sections.label: Autonomous universities in cybersecurity strategy
sections.summary: Four of Singapore's six autonomous universities are named in the Cybersecurity Strategy Paper as playing key roles in R&D and talent development.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Daniel Goh Pei Siong (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: In the Paper outlining Singapore’s Cybersecurity Strategy, four of our six autonomous universities are named as playing key roles in fostering cutting-edge research and development (R&D) and talent development.

sections.label: SIT and SUTD cybersecurity programmes
sections.summary: SIT and SUTD offer Bachelor and Master's programmes in cybersecurity.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Daniel Goh Pei Siong (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: The Singapore Institute of Technology (SIT) and the Singapore University of Technology and Design (SUTD) offer Bachelor and Master's programmes in cybersecurity.

sections.label: CII owner incident notification duty
sections.summary: Section 14(1)(b) requires a CII owner to notify the Commissioner of a cybersecurity incident in any interconnected or communicating computer under the owner's control.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Daniel Goh Pei Siong (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: First, section 14(1)(b) specifies that the owner of a CII must notify the Commissioner of a cybersecurity incident in any computer or computer system under the owner’s control that is interconnected with or that communicates with the CII.

sections.label: Mandatory reporting to CSA proposal
sections.summary: The only way forward might be to legislate mandatory reporting of all cybersecurity incidents to CSA with assured confidentiality and indemnity.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Daniel Goh Pei Siong (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: The only way forward might be to legislate mandatory reporting of all cybersecurity incidents to CSA with the assurance of confidentiality and indemnity.

sections.label: Cybersecurity spend ranking and PAC report
sections.summary: Singapore ranked third globally in cybersecurity spend at 0.22% of GDP, and the PAC reported public sector IT control problems from agencies not complying.

sentences.speaker: Ms Joan Pereira (Tanjong Pagar)
sentences.text: Last year, we ranked third globally in terms of cybersecurity spend as a percentage of gross domestic product (GDP) with 0.22%, behind Israel (0.35%) and the UK (0.26%).

sentences.speaker: Ms Joan Pereira (Tanjong Pagar)
sentences.text: Just last month, the Public Accounts Committee (PAC) reported IT control problems in our public sector due to "agencies not complying with the controls put in place".

sections.label: Supply chain systems not CII
sections.summary: CSA clarified in its public consultation report that computer systems in the supply chain supporting a CII's operation will not be designated as CII.

sentences.speaker: Ms Joan Pereira (Tanjong Pagar)
sentences.text: CSA had clarified in its report on the public consultation on the draft Cybersecurity Bill that "computer systems in the supply chain supporting the operation of a CII will not be designated as CII".

sections.label: Voluntary accreditation regimes instead
sections.summary: Due to practical difficulties for global cybersecurity service providers deploying employees worldwide at short notice, CSA will work with industry and professional association partners on voluntary accreditation regimes instead.

sentences.speaker: Ms Joan Pereira (Tanjong Pagar)
sentences.text: Due to concerns that this will pose practical difficulties for global cybersecurity service providers since they deploy employees from different parts of the world to deliver urgent services at short notice, CSA has decided to work with industry and professional association partners to establish voluntary accreditation regimes instead.

sections.label: Password management survey finding
sections.summary: One in three respondents did not manage their passwords securely.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ganesh Rajaram (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: One in three respondents did not manage their passwords securely.

sections.label: Respondents' security practices
sections.summary: One in three respondents did not enable two-factor authentication, and almost half did not conduct virus scans on their devices and files.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ganesh Rajaram (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: One in three respondents did not enable their two-factor authentication.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ganesh Rajaram (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: Despite widespread use of cloud storage, mobile and other storage devices, almost half the respondents did not conduct virus scans on their devices and files.

sections.label: Projected cybercrime cost
sections.summary: A commentary projected the cost of security failure from cybercrime to grow to over US$2 trillion globally in 2018.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ganesh Rajaram (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: According to a commentary on channelnewsasia.com last December, the cost of security failure because of cybercrime is projected to grow to over US$2 trillion globally in 2018.

sections.label: Singapore internet and social media use
sections.summary: Singapore's internet penetration is 82.2%, and 70% of Singaporeans are active on social media, double the global average of 34%.

sentences.speaker: Mr Darryl David (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: Internet penetration rate in Singapore is at 82.2%, much higher than the global average, and 70% of Singaporeans are active on a social media platform, more than double the global average of 34%.

sections.label: CSA warning and Cybersecurity Bill
sections.summary: The CSA warned of a consistent effort to penetrate Government IT systems, making the Cybersecurity Bill needed and timely.

sentences.speaker: Mr Darryl David (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: What is more foreboding is the CSA warning that there has been a consistent and concerted effort to penetrate our Government’s IT system.

sentences.speaker: Mr Darryl David (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: Thus, the introduction of the Cybersecurity Bill is not only much needed, it is also timely.

sections.label: Cybersecurity Commissioner designating CIIs
sections.summary: Part 3 of the Bill gives the Cybersecurity Commissioner authority to designate computers and systems as CIIs and greater oversight.

sentences.speaker: Mr Darryl David (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: Part 3 of the Bill has vested the Cybersecurity Commissioner with the authority to designate computers and computer systems as CIIs and empower the cybersecurity office with greater oversight over these systems.

sections.label: Hacking, fake news, CMA questions
sections.summary: The passage asks how Government would deal with hackers or fake SPF sites, and how the Bill complements CMA legislation.

sentences.speaker: Mr Darryl David (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: For example, if someone hacks into the Singapore Police Force (SPF) website or creates a fake SPF site to spread fake news of terror acts, how would the Government deal with the perpetrators and the ensuing chaos that possibly could result from this cybercrime?

sentences.speaker: Mr Darryl David (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: Fake news, as we all know, can lead to widespread panic that erodes the trust in public institutions.

sentences.speaker: Mr Darryl David (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: So, can the cybersecurity office hold the perpetrators of such cybercrimes responsible for the consequences of their crimes?

sentences.speaker: Mr Darryl David (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: Or will the crimes fall under other legislation, such as the CMA?

sentences.speaker: Mr Darryl David (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: And, if so, how can the Cybersecurity Bill complement the legislation under CMA?

sections.label: Cyber terrorism deaths and Bill support
sections.summary: The speaker says cyber terrorists can cause hundreds of thousands or millions of deaths and supports the Government's cybersecurity Bill.

sentences.speaker: Mr Darryl David (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: At worst, cyber terrorists can cause the deaths of hundreds of thousands, if not, millions of innocents.

sentences.speaker: Mr Darryl David (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: I thus believe that it is timely that the Government is taking steps to address the critical issue of cybersecurity and I stand in firm support of this Bill.

sections.label: MINDEF hack, WannaCry, Petya incidents
sections.summary: The passage lists the 2017 MINDEF hack, the WannaCry ransomware attack and the Petya attack as cybersecurity incidents.

sentences.speaker: Mr Azmoon Ahmad (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: Unfortunately, our MINDEF was hacked on 1 February 2017 where details of some of our Servicemen and personnel, including their Singapore NRIC numbers, telephone numbers, and birth dates were leaked.

sentences.speaker: Mr Azmoon Ahmad (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: On 14 May 2017, ransomware "WannaCry" crippled the world for three consecutive days and compromised more than 3,000 systems globally.

sentences.speaker: Mr Azmoon Ahmad (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: On 28 June 2017, "Petya", which was considered more dangerous than previously known ransomwares, created havoc as it encrypted the Master File Tree Tables for New Technology File System (NTFS), overwriting the Master Boot Record.

sections.label: Cybersecurity Bill framework welcome
sections.summary: The Cybersecurity Bill aims to establish a framework for managing and responding to cybersecurity threats, which the speaker welcomes.

sentences.speaker: Mr Azmoon Ahmad (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: It could even be far-reaching as the outreach from a cyberattack can be wide and endless.

sentences.speaker: Mr Azmoon Ahmad (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: Thus, the Cybersecurity Bill, which is aimed at establishing a working framework in the management of and in response to cybersecurity threats, is very much welcome.

sections.label: Quann survey and ASEAN e-commerce
sections.summary: A Quann survey of 150 IT professionals found many lacked or did not practise incident response plans, and Singapore seeks an ASEAN e-commerce platform.

sentences.speaker: Mr Kwek Hian Chuan Henry (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: In a survey done last year by security services provider Quann of 150 senior IT professionals from Singapore, Hong Kong and Malaysia, it showed that 40% do not have an incident response plan when they are facing cyberattacks and 67% of those who had those plans admitted to not practising their incident response plans.

sentences.speaker: Mr Kwek Hian Chuan Henry (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: As Chair of ASEAN this year, Singapore has identified our aspirations to push for an ASEAN-wide e-commerce platform.

sections.label: Due diligence and certification for cyber professionals
sections.summary: The passage proposes more thorough due diligence checks on cybersecurity professionals and a certification system favouring those with roots in Singapore.

sentences.speaker: Mr Kwek Hian Chuan Henry (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: One, more thorough due diligence checks by our cybersecurity agencies on professionals.

sentences.speaker: Mr Kwek Hian Chuan Henry (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: Three, create a certification system that favours cyber professionals who have a vested interest in Singapore, people who have some real roots and deep roots in Singapore, rather than fly-by-night experts who drop by for ad hoc projects whom our laws have difficulty to reach and deter.

sections.label: Rise in Singapore cybercrimes
sections.summary: Cybercrimes rose from 7.9% of overall crimes in 2014 to 14% in 2016, with CMCA cases more than doubling from 280 to almost 700.

sentences.speaker: Asst Prof Mahdev Mohan (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: In Singapore, there has been a reported increase in the proportion of cybercrimes to overall crimes from 7.9% in 2014 to 14% in 2016.

sentences.speaker: Asst Prof Mahdev Mohan (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: Cases reported under the Computer Misuse and Cybersecurity Act (CMCA) more than doubled from 280 in 2015 to almost 700 in 2016, with ransomware, hacking and the compromise of online accounts, such as Facebook, SingPass and Internet banking accounts, figuring most prominently amongst these.

sections.label: Public consultation submissions received
sections.summary: A public consultation held from 10 July to 24 August 2017 received close to a hundred submissions from diverse stakeholders.

sentences.speaker: Asst Prof Mahdev Mohan (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: Conducted between 10 July 2017 and 24 August 2017, the public consultation exercise garnered close to a hundred submissions from a diverse range of stakeholders.

sections.label: US cybersecurity rule implementation costs
sections.summary: US data showed company costs of up to US$150,000 for independent assessments and up to US$350,000 for continuous monitoring equipment.

sentences.speaker: Asst Prof Mahdev Mohan (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: Data disclosed during a recent proposal to amend the Homeland Security Acquisition Regulation in the US had revealed that costs per company associated with implementing its cybersecurity rules went up to US$150,000 for independent assessments, and equipment costs ranging, in turn, for up to US$350,000 to perform continuous monitoring for this purpose.

sections.label: UK information sharing and regional cybercrime
sections.summary: The UK's Cybersecurity Information Sharing Partnership lets organisations voluntarily report incidents, and the speaker asks about regional and international action.

sentences.speaker: Asst Prof Mahdev Mohan (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: Or the UK’s Cybersecurity Information Sharing Partnership, a structure for incident disclosure and collection which, among other things, allows business organisations to work in collaboration with the regulators to collaboratively and voluntarily report incidents to the UK national computer emergency response team?

sentences.speaker: Asst Prof Mahdev Mohan (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: Allow me to end by noting that the Economist Intelligence Unit's most recent report notes that cybercriminals are seeking out points of least resistance in the Asia Pacific region.

sentences.speaker: Asst Prof Mahdev Mohan (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: So, now we are going to have cybercrime legislation in addition to CMCA.

sentences.speaker: Asst Prof Mahdev Mohan (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: But jurisdictions, perhaps as in our neighbouring jurisdictions, without this cybercrime legislation or with weak enforcement, are attracting cybercriminals as vantage points from which to conduct attacks into the networks of more advanced countries.

sentences.speaker: Asst Prof Mahdev Mohan (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: So, if I can end by just asking if the Minister could share anything that is going to be done regionally and perhaps internationally to prevent this.

sections.label: NETS outage and licensing framework
sections.summary: After a NETS outage affected thousands, the speaker asks whether the proposed licensing framework would impact Singapore's cybersecurity ecosystem.

sentences.speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye (Tanjong Pagar)
sentences.text: Just last Friday, thousands of Singaporeans were affected when the e-payment system Network for Electronic Transfers (NETS) was down for more than an hour.

sentences.speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye (Tanjong Pagar)
sentences.text: Our Smart Nation needs to be secured all the time, every time.

sentences.speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye (Tanjong Pagar)
sentences.text: However, I would like to ask if the proposed licensing framework would impact the development of a vibrant cybersecurity ecosystem in Singapore.

sections.label: Cybersecurity professionals needed
sections.summary: The speaker asks the Minister for insights on the number of cybersecurity professionals needed over the next five to 10 years.

sentences.speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye (Tanjong Pagar)
sentences.text: Can the Minister provide some insights on the number of cybersecurity professionals needed for the next five to 10 years?

sections.label: White hat hackers as short-term solution
sections.summary: The speaker suggests using white hat hackers while professionals are trained, noting MINDEF invited 300 hackers to find vulnerabilities.

sentences.speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye (Tanjong Pagar)
sentences.text: Perhaps, a short-term solution in ensuring that our cybersecurity defences are working as intended, while current batches of cybersecurity professionals are still being trained in schools, would be through the use of “white hat” hackers.

sentences.speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye (Tanjong Pagar)
sentences.text: I have read with interest that MINDEF has recently invited 300 international and local hackers to hunt for vulnerabilities in its Internet-connected systems.

sections.label: CII owner cybersecurity duties
sections.summary: The Bill requires CII owners to follow codes and standards, report incidents, audit, assess risk, join exercises, and prevent and investigate serious incidents.

sentences.speaker: Ms Jessica Tan Soon Neo (East Coast)
sentences.text: The measures outlined in this Bill are no different, requiring owners of CIIs to proactively put in place the right procedures to protect customer data and ensure quality and continuity of service.

sentences.speaker: Ms Jessica Tan Soon Neo (East Coast)
sentences.text: This Bill spells out the code of practice and standards of performance, the duty of owners of CIIs to report cybersecurity incidents; to perform cybersecurity audits and risk assessment of CIIs and also to participate in cybersecurity exercises; and put in place measures to prevent, manage and respond to threats and incidents; investigation and prevention of serious cybersecurity incidents.

sections.label: Penalties and government CII owners
sections.summary: Non-compliance carries penalties including up to two years' imprisonment, and for Government-owned CIIs the responsible Permanent Secretary is treated as owner.

sentences.speaker: Ms Jessica Tan Soon Neo (East Coast)
sentences.text: Failure of owners to comply with the regulations carries with it heavy penalties, including imprisonment for a term not exceeding two years.

sentences.speaker: Ms Jessica Tan Soon Neo (East Coast)
sentences.text: Clause 7(8) puts the same emphasis on CIIs owned by the Government, stating that when the CII is owned and operated by the Government, the Permanent Secretary allocated to the Ministry who has the responsibility for the CII is treated as the owner.

sections.label: Breach discovery takes 12 months
sections.summary: Statistics and information show many breached organisations take about 12 months on average to discover the breach.

sentences.speaker: Ms Jessica Tan Soon Neo (East Coast)
sentences.text: In fact, statistics and information tell us that many oganisations that have been breached take about 12 months, on average, to actually discover that they are breached.

sections.label: Ongoing cybersecurity journey
sections.summary: The cybersecurity journey has started and requires continual work to protect essential services.

sentences.speaker: Ms Jessica Tan Soon Neo (East Coast)
sentences.text: The cybersecurity journey has started and is one that we have to continually work on to protect our essential services.

sections.label: Ponemon 2017 breach cost study
sections.summary: The Ponemon Institute's 2017 study found the average cost per lost or stolen sensitive record for 419 companies was about US$3.62 million.

sentences.speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
sentences.text: Yet, according to the Cost of Data Breach Study 2017 by the Ponemon Institute, a US-based organisation that conducts independent research on privacy, data protection and information security policy, the average cost for each lost or stolen record containing sensitive and confidential information for 419 companies which took part in the survey was approximately US$3.62 million.

sections.label: MP concerns on cybersecurity costs
sections.summary: A speaker raises concerns about cybersecurity investment costs, incentives, awareness, onerous CII reporting requirements, and removing licensing of individual professionals.

sentences.speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
sentences.text: I have heard from business operators who think they are adequately covered with an anti-virus software, for example.

sentences.speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
sentences.text: I hope the Government can look into the estimated costs that will be incurred in cybersecurity investments and consider financial incentives to alleviate the financial burden of implementing enhanced cybersecurity measures.

sentences.speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
sentences.text: Awareness and education would also go a long way in helping organisations make informed decisions.

sentences.speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
sentences.text: I wish to also express my concern that the incident reporting and investigation requirements on CII owners under the Bill could be too onerous, especially when they are potential victims of cyberattacks.

sentences.speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
sentences.text: Perhaps, for high-risk CIIs, the Commission could work more closely with the owners to improve prevention measures.

sentences.speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
sentences.text: I also note that with the decision to simplify the licensing framework, the Bill will do away with the licensing of individual cybersecurity professionals.

sections.label: Global data breaches and cybercrime damage
sections.summary: Globally there were more than 900 data breaches in the first six months of 2017, and analysts say cybercrime damage could hit US$6 trillion annually by 2021.

sentences.speaker: Mr Desmond Choo (Tampines)
sentences.text: In the first six months of 2017, globally, there were more than 900 data breaches in the first six months of last year.

sentences.speaker: Mr Desmond Choo (Tampines)
sentences.text: Analysts say that the damage caused by cybercrimes globally could hit US$6 trillion annually by 2021.

sections.label: MCI audit and risk assessment grants
sections.summary: MCI stated in its Report on the Consultation Outcome that it will not provide grants to offset costs of audits and risk assessments because they are regulatory requirements.

sentences.speaker: Mr Desmond Choo (Tampines)
sentences.text: In the Report on the Consultation Outcome paper released by the Ministry of Communications and Information (MCI), it was stated that MCI will not be providing grants to offset the costs of audits and risk assessments because they are regulatory requirements.

sections.label: Singapore ranked top cyberattack launch spot
sections.summary: In 2017, Check Point Software Technologies ranked Singapore as the world's top spot to launch global cyberattacks from.

sentences.speaker: Mr Desmond Choo (Tampines)
sentences.text: On a separate but related matter, in 2017, data security firm Check Point Software Technologies ranked Singapore as the world's top spot to launch global cyberattacks from.

sections.label: Support for cybersecurity Bill
sections.summary: The speaker says the Bill puts us in the right direction for hardening systems and supports it as important for strengthening cybersecurity laws.

sentences.speaker: Mr Desmond Choo (Tampines)
sentences.text: In spite of the concerns, this Bill puts us in the right direction in hardening our systems for both current and future security needs.

sentences.speaker: Dr Intan Azura Mokhtar (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: I support the Bill, which is an important one that will eventually help strengthen our laws on cybersecurity and related threats.

sections.label: Government ensuring company integrity and reliability
sections.summary: The passage asks how the Government plans to ensure the integrity and reliability of these companies.

sentences.speaker: Dr Intan Azura Mokhtar (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: How does the Government plan to ensure the integrity and reliability of these companies?

sections.label: Bill needs non-legislative approaches
sections.summary: The Bill addresses measures and countermeasures for cybersecurity threats and incidents in the public sector and Civil Service but must be accompanied by non-legislative approaches.

sentences.speaker: Dr Intan Azura Mokhtar (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: Third, while this Bill aims to address the various measures and countermeasures to prevent, manage and respond to cybersecurity threats and incidents that may afflict our public sector and Civil Service, it must be accompanied by non-legislative approaches as well.

sections.label: Support for the Bill
sections.summary: The speaker states that despite concerns, he supports the Bill.

sentences.speaker: Dr Intan Azura Mokhtar (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: Notwithstanding my concerns above, I support this Bill, Mr Speaker.

sections.label: ESET online precautions survey
sections.summary: A 2015 ESET survey found 76% of Singaporeans know online precautions but only 44% act on them.

sentences.speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: A 2015 survey published by IT Security firm ESET notes that although 76% of Singaporeans know of some precautions to take when going online, only 44% actually do anything about it.

sections.label: Singapore share of global malware
sections.summary: Singapore hosts 1.6% of the world's malware despite its small share of world population.

sentences.speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: Singapore hosts 1.6% of all the malware in the world, which is an astronomical amount considering that our island holds only a very small fraction of the world's population.

sections.label: QBE survey of SMEs
sections.summary: A QBE survey found 23% of surveyed SMEs concerned about sensitive data security and 35% of smaller SMEs without cyber protection.

sentences.speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: A recent survey conducted by QBE insurance found that only 23% of all surveyed SMEs are concerned about security of sensitive data while 35% of smaller SMEs have no cyber protection at all.

sections.label: CSA preventative measures and breaches
sections.summary: CSA could identify trends and take preventative measures rather than wait for a CII attack, preventing unreported incidents.

sentences.speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: Rather than waiting for a CII to be attacked, CSA might be able to identify trends and take preventative measures.

sentences.speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: This will also prevent incidents from going unreported, for example, like the Equifax breach in the US, which resulted in the sensitive data of 145 million citizens being stolen, or Uber paying off hackers who had stolen customer information.

sections.label: Singapore phishing attack ranking
sections.summary: A CyberInt study ranked Singapore fifth biggest global target for phishing attacks after the US, Britain, the Philippines and Russia.

sentences.speaker: Mr Patrick Tay Teck Guan (West Coast)
sentences.text: In another study by CyberInt, a cybersecurity threat monitor, Singapore ranked as the fifth biggest global target for phishing attacks, after the US, Britain, the Philippines and Russia.

sections.label: CII classification checks and support
sections.summary: Asks whether organisations can check with CSA if they are CII owners, and whether notified CIIs have support programmes for compliance.

sentences.speaker: Mr Patrick Tay Teck Guan (West Coast)
sentences.text: First, is there a mechanism in place to allow organisations to check with CSA if they are classified to be an owner of a CII?

sentences.speaker: Mr Patrick Tay Teck Guan (West Coast)
sentences.text: Second, for organisations which have been notified that they are a CII, are there any support programmes in place which they can tap on to tide them through the implementation of processes and infrastructure to enable compliance with the requirements of CIIs under the Bill?

sections.label: Wider community cyber preparedness
sections.summary: Asks whether plans exist to prepare the wider community, enterprises and individuals for cyber contingencies and mitigation.

sentences.speaker: Mr Patrick Tay Teck Guan (West Coast)
sentences.text: Fifth, recognising that cybersecurity is everyone’s responsibility, are there plans to ensure that the wider community, our enterprises and individuals, are prepared for cyber contingencies and know what to do to prevent one, or, when faced with one, what to do to mitigate its impact?

sections.label: SME costs, innovation, education
sections.summary: Raises concerns about compliance cost for SMEs, whether the Act curtails innovation, and hopes for a continuing education framework.

sentences.speaker: Mr Patrick Tay Teck Guan (West Coast)
sentences.text: First, I am worried about the additional compliance cost.

sentences.speaker: Mr Patrick Tay Teck Guan (West Coast)
sentences.text: Are there any grants to help SMEs cope with this extra cost?

sentences.speaker: Mr Patrick Tay Teck Guan (West Coast)
sentences.text: Second, will the new Act curtail innovation from the companies?

sentences.speaker: Mr Patrick Tay Teck Guan (West Coast)
sentences.text: Third, as the cybersecurity scene changes every day, individuals and companies must upgrade and keep abreast with the latest developments.

sentences.speaker: Mr Patrick Tay Teck Guan (West Coast)
sentences.text: Hence, I hope that the industry can develop a continuing education framework.

sections.label: CII owners detect threats
sections.summary: The Bill requires CII owners to establish mechanisms and processes to detect cybersecurity threats.

sentences.speaker: Ms Sun Xueling (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
sentences.text: The Bill sets out requirements for CII owners to establish mechanisms and processes to detect any cybersecurity threats.

sections.label: Assessment of business costs
sections.summary: Asks whether an assessment has been done on costs businesses would incur from implementing the Cybersecurity Bill.

sentences.speaker: Ms Sun Xueling (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
sentences.text: Has there been an assessment on the costs businesses would incur from the implementation of the Cybersecurity Bill?

sections.label: Commissioner can require information
sections.summary: The Bill empowers the Commissioner of Cybersecurity to require any person to surrender information on a suspected cyberattack.

sentences.speaker: Ms Sun Xueling (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
sentences.text: For example, the Bill empowers the Commissioner of Cybersecurity to require any person to surrender pertinent information regarding a suspected cyberattack.

sections.label: Cybersecurity Bill and existing legislation
sections.summary: The passage asks how the Cybersecurity Bill would interact with existing legislation that may already cover cybersecurity requirements.

sentences.speaker: Ms Sun Xueling (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
sentences.text: Lastly, how would the Cybersecurity Bill interact with existing legislation that may already cover cybersecurity requirements?

sections.label: Commissioner designating CII
sections.summary: The Bill allows the Commissioner to designate as CII computers and computer systems necessary for continuous delivery of essential services in Singapore.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim
sentences.text: The Bill allows the Commissioner to designate as CII, computers and computer systems necessary for the continuous delivery of essential services in Singapore.

sections.label: Systems outside Singapore jurisdiction
sections.summary: Singapore cannot control systems outside its jurisdiction by designating them as CII under the Bill.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim
sentences.text: While Singapore may be able to work with these international organisations to ensure the cybersecurity of the systems in question, we cannot control such systems by designating them as CII under the Bill as they are outside our jurisdiction.

sections.label: CII owners' responsibility
sections.summary: CII owners are ultimately responsible for the cybersecurity of their respective CII.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim
sentences.text: CII owners are ultimately responsible for the cybersecurity of their respective CII.

sections.label: Identifying CII systems
sections.summary: CIIs are computers and computer systems necessary for continuous delivery of essential services, whose loss would debilitate essential services in Singapore.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim
sentences.text: CIIs are identified as computers and computer systems that are necessary for the continuous delivery of essential services, the loss or compromise of which would have a debilitating effect on the availability of the essential services in Singapore.

sections.label: No action for compliant owners
sections.summary: The passage states no action is intended under the Bill against CII owners for cybersecurity breaches if they comply with their obligations.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim
sentences.text: As mentioned in my opening speech, we do not intend to take action under the Bill against CII owners for cybersecurity breaches so long as they comply with their obligations thereunder.

sections.label: Penalty for CII reporting non-compliance
sections.summary: Reporting CII cybersecurity incidents is required under clause 14, and non-compliance without reasonable excuse is an offence with a maximum penalty of $100,000, two years' imprisonment, or both.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim
sentences.text: As mentioned earlier, reporting cybersecurity incidents in respect of CII is a requirement under clause 14, and any non-compliance without reasonable excuse will be an offence.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim
sentences.text: The maximum penalty is $100,000, or two years' imprisonment, or both.

sections.label: CLIPS prepares CII owners
sections.summary: CSA developed the Cybersecurity Legislation Initialisation Programme for Sector Leads, or CLIPS, to work with CII sector regulators to prepare CII owners for their obligations under the Bill.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim
sentences.text: To assist CII owners and their staff in getting ready for the implementation of the Bill, CSA has developed a Cybersecurity Legislation Initialisation Programme for Sector Leads, also termed as CLIPS, to work with the CII sector regulators to prepare CII owners for their obligations under the Bill.

sections.label: Government bears national cybersecurity costs
sections.summary: Much of the cost of strengthening cybersecurity protection and enhancing responses at the national level is borne directly by the Government, including national infrastructure, manpower, exercises and NCIRT deployment.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim
sentences.text: Much of the cost of strengthening cybersecurity protection and enhancing responses to cybersecurity threats and incidents at the national level is borne directly by the Government.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim
sentences.text: This includes resourcing national-level cybersecurity infrastructure and manpower, conducting regular cybersecurity exercises to validate cybersecurity incident management processes, and deploying National Cyber Incident Response Teams (NCIRT) to respond to cybersecurity incidents.

sections.label: No funding for CII obligations
sections.summary: MCI and CSA will not provide funding to offset the costs of CII obligations, which are regulatory requirements.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim
sentences.text: As Mr Ganesh Rajaram mentioned, cybersecurity will actually help companies protect their bottom line.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim
sentences.text: Therefore, on balance, MCI and CSA will not provide funding to offset the costs of CII obligations which are regulatory requirements.

sections.label: Bill applies with other laws
sections.summary: The Bill will apply concurrently with other laws and regulations enacted in Singapore, including existing sectoral laws.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim
sentences.text: The Bill will apply concurrently with other laws and regulations enacted in Singapore, including existing sectoral laws.

sections.label: AC interaction and information use limits
sections.summary: CII owners in banking and finance will interact with an AC, a senior officer appointed from MAS, and information shared with CSA under the Bill cannot be used for enforcement action under sectoral regulations.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim
sentences.text: For example, CII owners in the banking and finance sector will interact with an AC, who will be a senior officer appointed from MAS, for requirements under the Bill.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim
sentences.text: I want to highlight that information shared with CSA under the Cybersecurity Bill cannot be used for enforcement action against the CII owners under sectoral regulations.

sections.label: CII protection and cyber safety
sections.summary: The Bill provides for protection of CII in Singapore and ensures CII owners maintain cyber safety awareness, protection and vigilance against threats and incidents.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim
sentences.text: The Bill provides for the protection of the CII in Singapore and ensures that CII owners maintain a necessary level of cyber safety awareness, protection and vigilance against cybersecurity threats and incidents.

sections.label: Conditions for investigation action
sections.summary: Three conditions apply: necessity for the investigation, no less disruptive method, and consultation with the owner after weighing benefit against detriment.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim
sentences.text: The conditions are as follows: first, this is necessary for the purposes of the investigation; second, there is no less disruptive method of achieving the purpose of the investigation; and third, this can only be done after consultation with the owner, and having considered the importance of the computer to the business and operational needs of the owner, that the benefit of the action outweighs the detriment caused to the owner.

sections.label: Misuse offence and emergency powers
sections.summary: Misuse of information by the Commissioner or specified officers is a criminal offence, and clause 23 emergency powers are scoped to serious and imminent threats.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim
sentences.text: Misuse of the information by the Commissioner or other specified officers will be a criminal offence.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim
sentences.text: The powers under clause 23, which are for emergency cybersecurity measures, are not new and were taken from section 15A of CMCA.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim
sentences.text: We have also further scoped clause 23 to be tighter than the existing section 15A of CMCA, to make clear that action can only be taken against serious and imminent threats and not just any cyber threat to the national security, essential services, defence or the foreign relations of Singapore.

sections.label: Licensable cybersecurity services categories
sections.summary: Two categories, penetration testing and managed SOC monitoring, are licensable cybersecurity services, and all providers must be licensed.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim
sentences.text: Our focus is on more mainstream or mature cybersecurity services with the potential to cause significant impact on the overall cybersecurity landscape.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim
sentences.text: We have identified two categories of services, penetration testing and managed SOC monitoring, as licensable cybersecurity services, which are set out in the Second Schedule.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim
sentences.text: All providers of licensable cybersecurity services, regardless of whether they are companies or individuals directly engaged for such services or third-party vendors that support these companies, will need to be licensed.

sections.label: Records kept by service providers
sections.summary: Service providers must keep records of cybersecurity services provided to clients, including employee details, for not less than three years.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim
sentences.text: In addition, the service provider will be required to keep records on the cybersecurity services it has provided to its clients, including details of the employee providing the service, for not less than three years for accountability and traceability in the event of foul play.

sections.label: CSAT and CSPS programmes
sections.summary: CSAT partners industry and IHLs to attract graduates and convert professionals, while CSPS recruits and trains officers for deployment to public agencies.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim
sentences.text: For example, under the Cyber Security Associates and Technologists (CSAT) programme, CSA and the Infocomm Media Development Authority (IMDA) partner the industry and Institutes of Higher Learning (IHLs) to attract new graduates and convert existing professionals from related fields to a career in cybersecurity.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim
sentences.text: Under CSA’s Cybersecurity Professional Scheme (CSPS), officers will be recruited and trained in areas, such as cyber forensics and vulnerability assessment, before being deployed to public agencies overseeing CII sectors to assist companies in these sectors with their cybersecurity capabilities.

sections.label: Cybersecurity MOUs and ASEAN programme
sections.summary: Singapore signed cybersecurity MOUs with the US, UK, France and Australia, and launched an ASEAN Cyber Capacity Building Programme.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim
sentences.text: Bilaterally, we have signed Memorandums of Understanding (MOUs) with countries, such as the US, the UK, France and Australia, on cybersecurity cooperation and capability development.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim
sentences.text: Regionally, we have launched the Association of Southeast Asian Nations (ASEAN) Cyber Capacity Building Programme with ASEAN member states and Dialogue Partners to build cybersecurity capacity in the region.

sections.label: SMEs Go Digital cybersecurity support
sections.summary: SMEs can use IMDA's SMEs Go Digital programme to adopt cybersecurity solutions and get technical advice from the SME Digital Tech Hub.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim
sentences.text: In addition, SMEs can also tap on IMDA’s SMEs Go Digital programme to adopt cybersecurity solutions and seek technical advice on cybersecurity and other digital concerns from IMDA’s SME Digital Tech Hub.

sections.label: Responsible use protects cyberspace
sections.summary: If everyone uses computer systems and devices responsibly, collectively they can help protect Singapore's cyberspace.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim
sentences.text: If we each do our part to use our computer systems and devices responsibly, collectively, we can help to protect Singapore’s cyberspace.

sections.label: Ministry works with stakeholders
sections.summary: The Ministry will work with public and private stakeholders to keep laws robust and raise cybersecurity awareness and develop the ecosystem.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim
sentences.text: My Ministry will continue to work with stakeholders from the public and private sectors to ensure that our laws remain robust and relevant and, beyond this Bill, to raise the level of cybersecurity awareness and develop the cybersecurity ecosystem in Singapore.

sections.label: Legislation protects CII and services
sections.summary: Members will agree the legislation is important to protect CII and safeguard essential services from disruption by cyberattacks.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim
sentences.text: Members of the House will agree that it is an important legislation to protect our CII and safeguard our essential services from disruption by cyberattacks.
